root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `coolkey_fill_object()` may cache `new_obj_data` into the list, the lookup result for `obj->id` must resolve back to the current list node `obj`; otherwise the function assigns one allocation to a different list element as well.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original relies on `coolkey_find_object_by_id(&priv->objects_list, obj->id)` to recover the same object already being filled, but the inverted SimCList comparator can return a different list node. The fixed program restores the comparator contract and duplicate-ID hardening so the cache write stays attached to the current object only.

nodes.description: A later cleanup iteration reaches `free(o->data)` on the same aliased heap buffer, becoming the AddressSanitizer-reported second free.

nodes.state: One cleanup iteration frees the aliased heap buffer through `o->data`, leaving the twin list node with a dangling pointer.
The same `new_obj_data` pointer is written into both `obj_entry->data` and `obj->data`, creating shared ownership across two list nodes in `priv->objects_list`.

edges.relation: The list node pointer produced by `coolkey_find_object_by_id()` is the same `obj_entry` node later used at the shared-pointer store.
The heap pointer written at the shared-pointer store propagates unchanged to a later cleanup iteration and is freed once through `o->data`.
After one cleanup iteration frees the aliased buffer, a later iteration reaches the same `o->data` pointer again and executes the second free at the ASan sink.
